# A positive line trace is generated by its original section under a strict degree bound

Version3,2 October2026. [Focused whole-implication review](../../Research/audits/POSITIVE_SINGLE_SECTION_TRACE_AUDIT_2026_10_02.md) PASS. The general robust-generation criterion is retained; the full-rank q0 branch now has an exact projective finite-monodromy strengthening.

Let $X\xleftarrow hS\xrightarrow gY$ be TWO actual finite etale
maps from the SAME smooth connected projective source, of degrees
$n,\eta n$. Use the canonical etale identifications of the Cartier
bundles. Let $L\subset B_X$ be a line SUBBUNDLE of degree $a>0$,
with a nonzero original section s whose zero divisor has reduced
support of degree b. Let K and R be the complete actual first
traces of L and its original section image $O_X\cdot s$.
Put $r=\operatorname{rank}K$ and $k=\deg K$. Then
\[
\boxed{k<1+\frac{r(a-b)}{\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R=K}
\]
as actual integral subsheaves. In particular $k=1$ and $b<a$
imply exact generation by the original section. The proof does not
require a simultaneous Galois closure or a section descending
through the opposite map. The same criterion applies to other
bundles with specified compatible etale identifications, provided
the source L remains a line subbundle.

## The fixed positive q0 line

Retain BOTH actual finite etale maps $X\xleftarrow hS\xrightarrow gY$
from the SAME smooth connected projective source, with degrees $n,8n$
and the fixed original genus-nine exact section $q_0\theta$. Its raw
line is $O_X$, and its saturation in $B_X$ is $M=O_X(2O)$; the
section vanishes there exactly at $2O$. Let $R\subset K\subset B_Y$
be respectively the COMPLETE actual traces of the raw line and its
saturation M.

The rank of K is at least two. If $\deg K=1$, then
\[
\boxed{R=K\quad\text{as actual integral subsheaves}.}
\]
This assertion holds for each possible rank two, three or four,
without any assumption about a simultaneous Galois closure. It is
not asserted that $\deg K=1$ is automatic.

Let J be the complete first trace of the original three-section
image, and suppose $\deg J=1$. Write $t$ for its original contact
with the saturated X hyperplane, as in
[the contact theorem](first_section_contact_strictness.md).
In the additional branch $\deg K=1$, the following consequences hold:

- rank K two forces $t\ge11n$;
- rank K three forces $t\ge9n$;
- rank K four gives $K=J$, and J is strongly semistable of slope one
  quarter. Moreover $\operatorname{End}(J)$ is trivialized by a finite
  etale cover: on an actual one-leg closure followed by a tame
  eighth-torsion refinement,
  $q^*J=M_T^{\oplus4}$ with $M_T^8\simeq\omega_T$.

In this full-rank branch $(\det J)^2\otimes\omega_Y^{-1}$ is an
etale-trivializable degree-zero line; it is not asserted trivial on Y.
The finite-monodromy statement concerns End(J). J itself has positive
degree and is not a finite degree-zero coefficient.

Thus $t<9n$ and $\deg K=1$ force the last branch. The separate
[contact-seven theorem](contact_seven_equality_exclusion.md) now excludes
that equality for MAIN. Larger trace degrees, higher contact and the
unmarked common-cover problem remain open. Positive degree and strong
semistability alone do not supply a compatible common finite coefficient.

[Proof](../../Proofs/cartier_and_spin/actual_positive_single_section_trace.md).
